strings.home.title: Redirect the Force. Control the Fight.
strings.home.sub: Ashihara Karate is a full-contact martial art that turns an opponent's power against them through circular movement — sabaki. Under the Türkiye organisation we bring together discipline, courage, and respect.
strings.prin.title: The Three Pillars of Sabaki
strings.prin.1.d: Step off the line of attack with circular movement. Answer force with angle, not with force.
strings.prin.2.d: Move to the opponent's blind side and seize their balance. Good position is half the fight won.
strings.prin.3.d: The moment control is yours, finish with a decisive, economical technique. This is Ashihara's signature.
strings.hteaser.title: A School Born From Real Combat
strings.hteaser.p1: Starting from the Kyokushin tradition, Kanchō Hideyuki Ashihara built a plain, effective system suited to real fighting conditions. It prioritises function over show.
strings.hteaser.p2: In Türkiye we carry this legacy forward in a safe, disciplined, and supportive environment for children, teens, and adults alike.
strings.about.title: Discipline, Movement, Honour
strings.about.sub: Our sabaki philosophy, distance control, and dojo values.
strings.about.origin.title: The Sabaki Philosophy
strings.about.origin.p1: Ashihara Karate (Ashihara Kaikan) was founded in 1980 by Kanchō Hideyuki Ashihara. After years of training in Kyokushin karate, Ashihara created his own school focused on techniques that work in a real confrontation.
strings.about.origin.p2: At the heart of the system is 'sabaki': evading an attack with circular movement, moving to the opponent's blind spot, and countering the instant their balance breaks. This approach lets even smaller athletes gain the upper hand against stronger opponents.
strings.about.origin.p3: Ashihara's teaching is known for turning kata from abstract movements into directly applicable fighting scenarios.
strings.about.maai.title: The Three Distances of Sabaki (Maai)
strings.about.maai.1.d: The closest range to the opponent — a position from which a circular step can flow straight into a counter.
strings.about.maai.2.d: Neither too close nor too far — the middle distance where sabaki movement is applied most often.
strings.about.maai.3.d: Just outside the opponent's striking range — the distance that buys timing and positional advantage.
strings.about.history.title: Two Historical Journeys
strings.about.history.sub: Explore Ashihara Karate's global story and its journey in Türkiye.
strings.about.history.world.d: How Kanchō Hideyuki Ashihara's school was born in Japan and spread across the world.
strings.about.history.tr.d: Sensei Ziya Özkan's journey in Istanbul from 1983 to today.
strings.about.values.title: Our Values
strings.about.v1.d: Every session opens and closes with a bow. Respect for the opponent, the instructor, and yourself is essential.
strings.about.v2.d: Progress comes through repetition. A belt is not a destination but a journey.
strings.about.v3.d: Stepping outside the comfort zone builds strength on the mat and in life.
strings.whist.title: From Kyokushin to Sabaki
strings.whist.sub: How Hideyuki Ashihara's school was born in Japan and spread across the world.
strings.whist.origin.title: A Student of Kyokushin
strings.whist.origin.p1: Hideyuki Ashihara was born on 5 December 1944 in Hiroshima. In September 1961, at just 16, he joined the dojo of Kyokushinkai founder Mas Oyama.
strings.whist.origin.p2: On 26 March 1964, at 19, he earned his black belt (Shodan); he soon became an instructor and helped expand Kyokushinkai across western Japan.
strings.whist.founding.title: The Birth of Ashihara Kaikan
strings.whist.founding.p1: In September 1980, Hideyuki Ashihara founded the New International Karate Organisation (NIKO) — Ashihara Kaikan — at his own dojo in Matsuyama, taking the title 'Kanchō' (Grandmaster).
strings.whist.founding.p2: At the heart of the new school was 'sabaki': a system built on preparation, distance and timing judgement, and stance control — evading an attack in a circular motion and countering from the opponent's blind side.
strings.whist.spread.title: From Japan to the World
strings.whist.spread.p1: The school grew quickly and produced notable names, including Kazuyoshi Ishii, who became one of the creators of the K-1 kickboxing organisation.
strings.whist.spread.p2: Today NIKO maintains around 180 branches in Japan and more than 220 abroad, across Europe, the Americas, the Middle East, and Africa, with international championships and anniversary events held every year.
strings.whist.succession.title: A New Generation Leads
strings.whist.succession.p1: Diagnosed with ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) in 1987, Kanchō Ashihara appointed his senior student Hiroshi Harada in 1992 to oversee all of NIKO's affairs.
strings.whist.succession.p2: He passed away on 24 April 1995 at the age of 50; more than 1,000 people attended his funeral. His son, Hidenori Ashihara, became NIKO's second Kanchō at just 18 and still leads the organisation today.
strings.whist.succession.p3: After the Kanchō's passing, several senior students founded their own organisations, though all continue to share the same sabaki foundation.
strings.whist.tl.title: From Roots to Today
strings.whist.tl.1.d: A young Hideyuki Ashihara begins training at Mas Oyama's Kyokushinkai dojo.
strings.whist.tl.2.d: At 19, Ashihara earns his Shodan rank and soon becomes an instructor.
strings.whist.tl.3.d: In September 1980, NIKO — Ashihara Kaikan is formally founded, and the title of Kanchō is taken.
strings.whist.tl.4.d: Hideyuki Ashihara passes away on 24 April 1995; his son Hidenori Ashihara becomes the second Kanchō.
strings.whist.tl.5.d: NIKO today operates with 180 dojos in Japan and more than 220 abroad.
strings.thist.title: From Istanbul to Today
strings.thist.sub: Sensei Ziya Özkan's journey since 1983, and the story of Ashihara Karate in Türkiye.
strings.thist.official.p1: Ashihara Karate, introduced to Türkiye in 1986 by our master, Ferhat Özsert, is represented in Türkiye by Sensei Ziya Özkan, the sole official Branch Chief of NIKO (New International Karate Organisation)—currently the only official Ashihara Karate organisation headquartered in Japan. All official Ashihara Karate activities in Türkiye are conducted under the auspices of the Turkish Karate Federation.
strings.thist.sensei.title: Sensei Ziya Özkan
strings.thist.sensei.p1: Ziya Özkan was born in 1969, is married, and is the father of two. He began martial arts in 1983 with full-contact Kyokushin Karate; between 1983 and 1992 he fought in numerous unprotected full-contact matches, earning his first black belt in 1988.
strings.thist.sensei.p2: In 1991 he opened Türkiye's first professional Ashihara Karate gym in Ümraniye (Çakmak Mah.) — today's Ashihara Karate Istanbul Dojo — and has coached continuously in Istanbul ever since.
strings.thist.sensei.p3: He holds 3rd Dan from NIKO Japan and 7th Dan from the Turkish Karate Federation, teaching self-defence and fighting under Ashihara Karate.
strings.thist.sensei.quote: "In battle, it is not the fanciest weapon that matters — it's the one that works."
strings.thist.founding.title: The First Ashihara Dojo
strings.thist.founding.p1: In 1991, Ziya Özkan opened Türkiye's first professional Ashihara Karate dojo — today's Ashihara Karate Istanbul Dojo — in Ümraniye's Çakmak neighbourhood, and has coached there continuously ever since.
strings.thist.founding.p2: Today, classes run twice a week in small, dedicated groups at the sports hall of Halide Edip Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in the İnkılap neighbourhood.
strings.thist.recog.title: Over Three Decades of Work
strings.thist.recog.p1: Ziya Özkan holds 3rd Dan from NIKO Japan and 7th Dan from the Turkish Karate Federation, and also teaches self-defence and fighting under Ashihara Karate.
strings.thist.recog.p2: His participation in the school's 40th-anniversary celebrations reflected the strong ties between the Turkish representation and the international Ashihara community.
strings.thist.tl.title: The Istanbul Journey
strings.thist.tl.1.d: Ziya Özkan begins his martial arts journey in full-contact Kyokushin Karate.
strings.thist.tl.2.d: After years of full-contact matches, he earns his first black belt.
strings.thist.tl.3.d: Türkiye's first professional Ashihara Karate dojo opens in the Çakmak neighbourhood.
strings.thist.tl.4.d: The dojo continues teaching the discipline of sabaki to children, teens, and adults.
strings.thist.tl.5.d: Ashihara Karate Istanbul Dojo carries the Ashihara legacy forward in Türkiye.
